searchText: Sorry if this is already well known, but I'm wondering if there's an execution node that already has the latest API implemented? If so, it would be handy for testing on our end. If not, and it doesn't seem like it'll happen next week sometime, I could build a mock server. For a validator post-merge, would it make sense to run 1 consensus client, 2 execution client and a failure sensing MITM proxy in between to build a more resilient infra. If the MITM proxy heuristically senses a failure of an execution client it can switch to secondary client. MITM proxy can send PreparePayload requests to both exec clients and only request ExecutePayload on the primary execution client. MITM proxy can even use both exec clients in round robin to increase usage of less used client? Would it work and is it feasible? (I'm sorry if this channel is not right place to ask this) sounds a question for the ethstaker discord 😇 come join us https://discord.io/ethstaker FYI, There is a PR that suggests to hardcode terminal total difficulty into both, consensus and execution clients. It removes the complexity of handling dynamic TTD in consensus clients and prevents some edge cases. Also, it simplifies the mechanism preventing execution client to follow the wrong chain after transition in the case when the consensus counter party has failed or was misconfigured. - The PR https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2605 - Issue describing the complexity and edge cases https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/2603 <dankrad> I'm in favour of hardcoding it. Nobody should "accidentally" follow a PoW-fork It could be done by switching to PoS as the default operating mode but hardcoding TTD is less complex and more robust solution <@425572898787426305> What was the GitHub issue you linked in the call that talks about the risks of TTD stuff? this one? https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/2603 (and companion https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2605)

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
FYI, There is a PR that suggests to hardcode terminal total difficulty into both, consensus and execution clients. It removes the complexity of handling dynamic TTD in consensus clients and prevents some edge cases. Also, it simplifies the mechanism preventing execution client to follow the wrong chain after transition in the case when the consensus counter party has failed or was misconfigured. 

- The PR https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2605
- Issue describing the complexity and edge cases https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/2603

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <dankrad> I'm in favour of hardcoding it. Nobody should "accidentally" follow a PoW-fork

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: It could be done by switching to PoS as the default operating mode but hardcoding TTD is less complex and more robust solution
